subtitulo: Summarising culture shock for someone about to move
descripcion: Summarising is a mediation skill, not a comprehension skill: the test is whether your listener can now act, not whether you understood. At C1 the difficulty is selection under constraint — deciding what to drop, and being able to say what you dropped. The structural move is top-down: conclusion first, then two or three supports, then the caveat.

filas: Give me two minutes and I'll take you through it
*The short version is…* / *If you only remember one thing…*
Three things came out of it. First… Second… And the one that matters…
I'm skipping the methodology — ask if you want it
The sample was small, so treat it as directional
That's what they found. What I think about it is…

ejemplos.texto: *The short version is that the course works, but only for people who already have the basics.*
*I'm skipping the methodology. Ask me if you want it.*
*That's the finding. My own view is that they measured the wrong thing.*
*Three things came out of it. And the one that actually matters is the third.*
*The sample was small, so treat it as directional.*
*That's what they found. What I think about it is another matter.*

notas: Saying what you left out converts a lossy summary into a trustworthy one.
Keep reporting and evaluating separate. *They found X* and *I think X is wrong* must not blur.
The order events happened is almost never the right order to explain them.

es.en: Spanish has formulas for leading with the conclusion («en resumen», «lo esencial es…» – the bottom line is…), so the structure is available. The English expectation is to use it at the very top of the summary, not at the end.
es.es: El español tiene fórmulas para comenzar con la conclusión («en resumen, lo esencial es…» – «the bottom line is…»), por lo que la estructura ya está disponible. La expectativa en inglés es usarla al principio mismo del resumen, no al final.

de.en: «Das Wichtigste vorweg» corresponds exactly to the bottom line first, so leading with the answer is a familiar move. The formulas transfer directly.
de.de: «Das Wichtigste vorweg» entspricht genau der Idee von «the bottom line first», daher ist das Voranstellen der Antwort vertraut. Die Formulierungen lassen sich direkt übertragen.

it.en: «Il punto chiave è…» corresponds well to the bottom line is…, so leading with the answer is available. The English expectation is to place it at the very top.
it.it: «Il punto chiave è…» corrisponde bene a «the bottom line is…», quindi iniziare con la risposta è una strategia disponibile. In inglese ci si aspetta che compaia proprio all'inizio.

fr.en: «L'essentiel, c'est que…» corresponds well to the bottom line is…, so leading with the answer is available. The English expectation is to place it at the very top.
fr.fr: «L'essentiel, c'est que…» correspond bien à «the bottom line is…», donc commencer par la réponse est un mouvement disponible. En anglais, on attend cette formule tout en haut.

pt.en: «O essencial é…» corresponds well to the bottom line is…, so leading with the answer is available. The English expectation is to place it at the very top.
pt.pt: «O essencial é…» corresponde bem a «the bottom line is…», então começar pela resposta é uma opção disponível. A expectativa em inglês é colocá-la logo no início.

errores: Chronological retelling instead of a summary.
*Resume* meaning *summarise* — false friend; it means to restart.
Compressing by removing words rather than content: dense and unreadable.
Losing hedging in compression, turning a tentative finding into a fact.

es: «*Cabe destacar que*» rendered as *It fits to highlight that* instead of *It is worth noting that*.
de: «*Hervorzuheben ist*» rendered as *To highlight is* instead of *It is worth highlighting that*.
it: «*Va detto che*» rendered as *It goes said that* instead of *It should be said that*.
fr: «*Il convient de noter*» rendered as *It convenes to note* instead of *It is worth noting*.
pt: «*Importa referir*» rendered as *It imports to refer* instead of *It is worth mentioning*.

mision.consigna: Summarise what you've learned about adapting to a new country for someone moving next month.
requisitos: one sentence saying what you left out and why
use *a sense of belonging*, *cultural baggage* and *to acclimatise*

microtareas.texto: Write your advice as one sentence. Then three supports.
Say what you'd leave out about *romanticising a place*.
Record 90 seconds: *If you only remember one thing about culture shock…*

autochequeo: Is my conclusion in the first two sentences?
Did I retell chronologically instead of summarising?
Did I say what I left out?
Did compression turn any tentative finding into a flat fact?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on summarising. (1) Is the conclusion in the first two sentences? (2) Did I retell chronologically instead of summarising? (3) Did compression turn a tentative claim into a fact? (4) Where would someone with no background get lost? Do not rewrite the text.
